title: Smooth common fixed schemes of dense subgroups of linearly reductive groups
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Let $G$ be a smooth affine finite-type $k$-group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. An algebraic representation on a finite-dimensional $k$-vector space $V$ is a group-scheme homomorphism to $\operatorname{GL}(V)$, where $\operatorname{GL}(V)(A)$ is the group of invertible $A$-linear endomorphisms of $V\otimes_k A$. A group is linearly reductive if every finite-dimensional algebraic representation is a direct sum of simple representations; simple means nonzero with no nonzero proper invariant $k$-subspace, and invariant means preserved after every commutative $k$-algebra extension. Assume that $G$ is linearly reductive. Let $\Gamma\subset G(k)$ be an abstract subgroup whose rational points are Zariski dense in the underlying topological space of $G$. Let $X$ be a smooth affine finite-type $k$-scheme [def-pc-scheme], and let $a:G\times_kX\to X$ be a group action, that is, a morphism satisfying $a(1,x)=x$ and $a(g_1g_2,x)=a(g_1,a(g_2,x))$ after every commutative $k$-algebra extension [def-pc-fibre-product]. Suppose a closed subscheme $F\hookrightarrow X$ [def-weil-closed-immersion] represents the functor $$F(A)=\{x\in X(A):a(\gamma_A,x)=x\text{ for every }\gamma\in\Gamma\},$$ where $\gamma_A$ is the image of $\gamma$ in $G(A)$. Then $F$ is smooth over $k$. Neither $G$ nor $X$ is required to be connected.

source.place: Lemma 13.6 and Theorem 13.7, printed p.256, specialized to an algebraically closed field, an affine smooth scheme and a dense abstract subgroup. The local proof does not require connectedness or irreducibility of X.

proof.text: Write $X=\operatorname{Spec}B$. By [def-weil-closed-immersion], $F=\operatorname{Spec}(B/I)$ for an ideal $I$. Images of finitely many algebra generators generate $B/I$, so $F$ is affine and finite type over $k$. By clause (1) of [lem-wf-affine-nullstellensatz-vanishing], every closed point of $F$ is $k$-rational. By [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-scheme-over-field-regular], every local ring of the smooth scheme $X$ is regular. Fix such a closed point $x\in F(k)$ and put $A=\mathcal O_{X,x}$, with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$.

source.place: Lemma 13.6, printed p.256, with Lemmas 13.3--13.4, printed p.255

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-dense-fixed-local-ideal-jets] to $G,\Gamma,X,F,x$. Its hypotheses use only the given smoothness of $G$, density of $\Gamma$, affine finite type of $X$, and the stated fixed functor. It identifies $\mathcal O_{F,x}$ with $A/J$, where $J=(\gamma^*f-f:\gamma\in\Gamma,f\in\mathfrak m)\subseteq\mathfrak m$. For each $n\geq1$ it gives the finite-dimensional rational $G$-algebra $R_n=A/\mathfrak m^{n+1}$ and the equivariant surjection $q_n:M_n=\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^{n+1}\twoheadrightarrow V=\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2$. Inverse pullbacks are used, which give the same common-fixed ideal since $\Gamma$ is closed under inversion.

source.place: Lemma 13.6, printed p.256, with Lemmas 13.3--13.4, printed p.255

proof.text: Linear reductivity, as defined in the statement, makes $V$ and every $M_n$ finite direct sums of simple rational $G$-modules. By [lem-sfb-dense-restriction-semisimple], their restrictions to $\Gamma$ are semisimple and $q_n$ has a $\Gamma$-equivariant linear section. Decompose $V=V_0\oplus V_1\oplus\cdots\oplus V_r$, collecting the trivial simple summands in $V_0$ and taking each $V_i$ for $i>0$ to be a nontrivial simple $\Gamma$-module. Put $d=\dim_k V$ and $s=\sum_{i>0}\dim_k V_i$. For fixed $n$, let $W_i$ be the image of $V_i$ under the section. Thus $q_n:W_i\to V_i$ is an equivariant isomorphism and $W_0$ is fixed pointwise.

source.place: Lemma 13.6, printed p.256, with Lemmas 13.3--13.4, printed p.255

proof.text: For $i>0$, let $D_i\subseteq W_i$ be the span of $\gamma^*w-w$ for $\gamma\in\Gamma$ and $w\in W_i$. This is $\Gamma$-invariant: $h^*(\gamma^*w-w)=((h\gamma)^*w-w)-(h^*w-w)$. It is nonzero because $W_i$ is nontrivial. Simplicity gives $D_i=W_i$. Consequently every $W_i$ with $i>0$ lies in the image $J_n$ of $J$ in $R_n$: lift $w$ to $f\in\mathfrak m$, so $\gamma^*w-w$ is the image of $\gamma^*f-f$. Choose bases of the $W_i$, numbering all $i>0$ basis vectors first as $w_1,\ldots,w_s$ and the remaining ones as $w_{s+1},\ldots,w_d$. Lift them to $u_1,\ldots,u_d\in\mathfrak m$. Their classes form a basis of $V$.

source.place: Lemma 13.6, printed p.256, with Lemmas 13.3--13.4, printed p.255

proof.text: These $w_j$ generate $R_n$ as a $k$-algebra. Indeed a class in $\mathfrak m$ is a constant linear combination of the $u_j$ modulo $\mathfrak m^2$; in a product of $a$ elements of $\mathfrak m$, make this replacement in each factor to express it as a homogeneous polynomial of degree $a$ modulo $\mathfrak m^{a+1}$. Iterating for $a=1,\ldots,n$ expresses every element of $R_n$ as a polynomial in the $w_j$ plus its residue in $k$. Let $L_n=(w_1,\ldots,w_s)\subseteq R_n$. Step 4 gives $L_n\subseteq J_n$. The subspace $W_1\oplus\cdots\oplus W_r$ is invariant, so $L_n$ is invariant under every $\gamma^*$. The quotient $R_n/L_n$ is generated by scalars and the images of $W_0$, all fixed pointwise. Hence every $\gamma^*f-f$ maps to zero there, so $J_n\subseteq L_n$. We have proved $J+\mathfrak m^{n+1}=(u_1,\ldots,u_s)+\mathfrak m^{n+1}$.

source.place: Lemma 13.6, printed p.256, with Lemmas 13.3--13.4, printed p.255

proof.text: The integer $s$ depends only on the chosen decomposition of $V$, not on $n$. For every $n\geq1$, steps 3--5 give a tuple whose classes form a cotangent basis and whose first $s$ entries give the displayed ideal equality. Since $A$ is regular, [lem-sfb-regular-quotient-parameter-approximation] applies to $A,J,s$ and shows that $A/J$, hence $\mathcal O_{F,x}$, is regular. This includes $s=0$, $s=d$, and $d=0$; the tuples need not be compatible as $n$ varies.

source.place: Lemma 13.6, printed p.256, with Lemmas 13.3--13.4, printed p.255

proof.text: For every closed point $x$ of the finite-type affine scheme $F$, its residue field is $k$ and is therefore finite separable over $k$. Apply [lem-sfb-regular-separable-affine-smooth-neighbourhood] to the whole affine $F$ and the regular local ring just proved. This gives a smooth open neighbourhood $U_x$ of $x$. Let $U$ be their union. Its closed complement has no closed points of $F$, so is empty by [lem-sc-lft-over-field-jacobson-space]. Thus the $U_x$ cover $F$. By [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-local-on-source], $F$ is smooth over $k$. The same conclusion holds for empty $F$ by the empty-cover case of that node. No connectedness or irreducibility of either scheme was used.

source.place: Lemma 13.6, printed p.256, with Lemmas 13.3--13.4, printed p.255
